source_messages.body_text:
Tran Capital Management, an investment management company, released its second-quarter investor letter for its "Midcap Equity Strategy". The letter can be downloaded here. The Midcap Equity Strategy returned 16.9%, net of fees, in the second quarter, bringing year-to-date returns to 12.3%, compared with Bloomberg U.S. Mid Cap Index's 11.1% quarterly gains and 12.1% year-to-date returns. The S&P 500 returned 15.2% for the quarter and 10.2% year-to-date. After a challenging first quarter, patient, research-driven investing and selective additions during the selloff contributed meaningfully to performance. The firm remains constructive on its portfolio and the broader market, where returns appear supported by genuine earnings growth rather than multiple expansion. Additionally, reviewing the Fund's top five holdings could help identify its best picks for 2026.

In its second-quarter 2026 investor letter, Tran Capital Midcap Equity Strategy highlighted Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE). Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) designs and manufactures solid-oxide fuel cell systems for clean, reliable, on-site power generation, which positively contributed to the fund's returns this quarter. On September 23, 2026, Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) closed at $275.19 per share. Over the past month, Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) returned 18.57%, and its shares are up 276.01% over the past year. Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) has a market capitalization of $81.05 billion, and its stock has traded within a 52-week range of $61.37 to $351.28.

Tran Capital Midcap Equity Strategy stated the following regarding Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) in its Q2 2026 investor letter:

"Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) also contributed meaningfully to our performance. Electricity has become the binding constraint on the AI buildout. Operators can secure GPUs far faster than they can secure power, with grid interconnection queues now stretching for years. Bloom's solid oxide fuel cells address this bottleneck, delivering reliable on-site power in a fraction of the time it takes to wait on the grid (i.e. months, not years). We believe BE's solution is now cost-competitive with gas generation, as BE drives down cost each year. During the quarter, that value proposition translated into a landmark agreement with Oracle for up to 2.8 gigawatts of 1000 4th Street, Suite 800 | San Rafael, CA 94901 415.461.800 | info@trancapital.com trancapital.com | 2 fuel cell capacity, with an initial 1.2 gigawatts already contracted and deploying, validating BE's technology. BE reported 1Q26 revenue that more than doubled year-over-year and the company swung firmly to GAAP profitability. Management raised full-year guidance to roughly 80% growth at the midpoint."

Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. According to our database, 116 hedge fund portfolios held Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) at the end of the second quarter, up from 91 in the previous quarter. While we acknowledge the potential of Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock.

In another article, we discussed Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) and shared Carillon Eagle Small Cap Growth Fund's views on the contributor. In addition, please check out our hedge fund investor letters Q2 2026 page for more investor letters from hedge funds and other leading investors.

1 story1 Oracle Bonds Hit Record 8.31% Yield on $120B Junk Downgrade Risk↩︎ AI Sep 24, 2:13 PM EDT 82/44 
 Credit markets are increasingly pricing in a downgrade to junk status for Oracle, a move that would automatically remove $120B of the company's bonds from investment grade indexes. Long-term bond yields climbed to a new record of 8.31% this week, while five-year credit default swaps hit record highs of 237 basis points. Such a downgrade would expand the total junk bond market by roughly 10%. Simultaneously, $18B in construction loans tied to the company's Project Jupiter facility are now trading at approximately 89 cents on the dollar.
The escalation in borrowing costs follows Oracle's decision to issue a force majeure notice to Blue Owl Capital, the developer of its New Mexico AI data center built for OpenAI. Oracle is seeking the right to defer lease payments if the site misses its 2028 opening after state officials twice denied permits for a 17 mile gas pipeline required for power. S&P currently rates the company's debt at BBB-, one notch above junk. Morgan Stanley noted that this credit stress is putting other AI infrastructure debt under scrutiny, potentially raising financing costs for other hyperscalers.

若Oracle被降级至垃圾级，将使垃圾债券市场总规模扩大约10%。

title.value: Nebius Stock Is Soaring. A Partnership With Bloom Energy Solves This AI Dilemma.

source_messages.body_text:
Key Points

Nebius Group will use Bloom Energy’s fuel-cell systems to power its data centers, with 328 megawatts operational this year.

Nebius will pay up to $2.6 billion over the term of the agreement, which is expected to come on in three phases, each with a supply term of 10 years.

The partnership addresses AI’s high power demand, using ‘behind-the-meter’ systems to reduce grid dependence for data centers.

Artificial-intelligence cloud provider Nebius Group is turning to fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy as tech companies look for alternatives to local electrical grids to help power their data centers.

Bloom Energy’s fuel-cell systems, which generate electricity without combustion, will provide electricity for Nebius, with 328 megawatts of installed capacity expected to be operational this year. Nebius will pay up to $2.6 billion over the term of the agreement, which is expected to come on in three phases, each with a supply term of 10 years.

Shares of Nebius rose 15% Thursday, having soared 407% over the last 12 months. Bloom Energy stock, which is up more than 1,400% in the last year, rose 10%. Bloom Energy jumped 8% on Wednesday, when the $2.6 billion figure first was released.

The Barron's Daily

Free Weekly Newsletter

A morning briefing on what you need to know in the day ahead, including exclusive commentary from Barron's and MarketWatch writers.

Electricity remains one of the most sought-after resources in AI, particularly for so-called neoclouds like Nebius. The neocloud model depends on building out and powering data centers as quickly as possible for customers in need of compute capacity.

Bloom Energy’s on-site systems will be “behind-the-meter,” meaning they aren’t dependent on power from the larger electrical grid. This setup reduces Nebius’ dependence on building new grid transmissions and shortens the timeline to power its facilities, the company said.

“Power remains a key constraint for AI infrastructure build-outs, ” said Andrey Korolenko, chief product and infrastructure officer at Nebius. Bloom Energy’s fuel cells, he added, offer clean power “on the timelines our customers need, with the availability AI workloads require.”

Bloom Energy stock has surged on this kind of AI demand. Since 2024, the company has notched new or expanded deals with neocloud competitor CoreWeave, cloud giant Oracle, and electricity generator American Electric Power.

Advertisement - Scroll to Continue

After multiple years of losses, Bloom Energy is on track to earn net income of $475 million in 2026, analysts forecast. Wall Street expects that figure to rise to over $1.2 billion in 2027 and $2.1 billion in 2028.

title.value: Grid manager delays data center power auction over concern on who gets the bill - Cleveland.com

source_messages.body_text:
COLUMBUS, Ohio -- A plan to add more power to the electric grid has been postponed after federal regulators raised concerns about who would pay for it.

PJM Interconnection, which manages the power grid for Ohio and 12 other states, had planned to open a special auction Wednesday. The goal was to buy more electricity for peak usage times like the dead of winter and hottest summer days.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission agreed PJM needed more power but said the operator “did not adequately ensure that the procurement’s costs will be allocated to the customers who drive its need.”

PJM already bought enough power for day-to-day demand during its regular auction this summer, but it fell short of the amount it wanted for emergencies.

FERC agreed that PJM needed a backstop. But it said the grid operator “did not adequately ensure that the procurement’s costs will be allocated to the customers who drive its need.”

FERC Commissioner Lindsay See put it more plainly.

“PJM must better ensure that the customers driving new costs bear appropriate responsibility for them and that existing customers are not left paying the bill instead,” See wrote in a statement.

That is where Ohio comes in.

PJM runs the regional grid, but states still play a major role in deciding how utilities charge different kinds of customers. Ohio has not adopted statewide rules that clearly put data-center-related costs on data centers.

The Office of the Ohio Consumers’ Counsel warned about that gap.

It told FERC months ago that PJM was counting on states to protect families, even though Ohio has not put those protections in place.

“Ohio families should not subsidize data center development,” said Rep. Tristan Rader, a Lakewood Democrat. “I support pausing PJM’s backstop auction until there are enforceable protections against sticking households and Ohio’s existing businesses with that bill.”

FERC suspended the auction for up to five months, but it could happen sooner if PJM submits fixes that regulators accept.

PJM said it is “reviewing the order and intends to work quickly to address the Commission’s remaining concerns.”
